description.value: A preliminary hybrid PET/MR study testing whether multimodal imaging based on the network degeneration hypothesis can separate individual patients with different neurodegenerative syndromes using support vector machine classification.

spans.text: The main question of this study is whether multimodal neuroimaging guided by the NDH can separate individual patients with different neurodegenerative syndromes.

description.value: A preliminary observational study of 40 patients with different neurodegenerative syndromes who underwent one hybrid PET/MR imaging session.

spans.text: To obtain initial evidence, we performed a preliminary study, which combines multimodal imaging on a hybrid PET/MR scanner following concepts of the NDH and applying canonical multivariate pattern classification.
Forty patients with dementia due to different neurodegenerative syndromes (20 AD, 11 bvFTD, 4 SD, 5 PNFA) were included in this hybrid PET/MR study.

spans.text: Classification results based on the voxelwise multimodal < DC, MET, VBM > vx values from a ROI in the primary motor cortex were 45% for AD versus others, 60% for bvFTD versus others, 90% for SD versus others, and 87.5% for PNFA versus others, which were significantly lower (P < 0.001) than accuracies for corresponding NDH-based ROIs, except of PNFA.
